samples.summary: Frontend YorkieDocStore: three of the newly-added bands (colSpan/rowSpan, the `cols` column-ratio attribute, and `stylesJson` sanitization) have no test, while the other five do
samples.evidence: The new `describe('bands the numeric attributes a peer can write')` block argues explicitly that this store is a *duplicate* parser with no shared test and no `tsc` lane, then covers only `fontSize`, the inline image size, cell `padding`, `rowHeights` and `listLevel`. The same diff also wires `normalizeTableSpan` into `treeNodeToCell` (colSpan/rowSpan), `parseColumnWidthsAttr` into `treeNodeToBlock`, and `sanitizeDocStyles` into `getStyles()` in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` — none of which any test exercises. Grepping the whole frontend test file for `rowSpan`/`colSpan` returns only pre-existing `applyCellSpan` write tests (lines 2719-2877) that write 2/3 and read them back, never an out-of-band value; `getStyles`/`stylesJson` return zero matches. The `rowSpan: Infinity` sink is the one the change itself calls the sharpest (`expandCellRangeForMerges`' fixed-point loop → permanently hung tab), so a band wired to the wrong field or dropped here in the copy that actually serves the live collaborative editor would ship undetected.
searchedFor: grep getStyles|setStyles in the same file (no matches)
read the added describe block in the diff

samples.summary: The `normalizeListLevel` calls added to the PDF painter, the table renderer and the peer cursor have no test at their own call sites
samples.evidence: `pdf-painter.ts` (two sites), `view/table-renderer.ts` and `view/peer-cursor.ts` all gained a raw→normalized level read. `packages/docs/test/model/list-level.test.ts` says so in its own comment ("the other three call sites the change normalized — the PDF painter, the table renderer and the peer cursor — ... are left to the unit test of the band itself"), and grepping `packages/docs/test/export` for `listLevel` finds only `docx-exporter.test.ts` and a `listLevel: 0`/`undefined` fixture — nothing that feeds a poisoned level to `PdfPainter`. Only `doc-canvas`/`paint-layout` is covered (editor-tab-bullet.test.ts 'a poisoned list level paints inside the page'). If one of these three were wired to the wrong variable, the exported PDF or the peer caret would silently paint at NaN coordinates with a green suite.

samples.summary: The `sanitizeDocStyles` wiring at the CRDT read boundary (`docsTreeToDocument`'s `stylesJson` parse) is untested; only the pure function is
samples.evidence: `sanitizeDocStyles` is unit-tested in `packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts`, but grepping `packages/docs/test` for `stylesJson` returns no matches, so nothing asserts that `docsTreeToDocument` actually routes the parsed registry through it (the same is true of the frontend `getStyles`). The module comment calls this the one string that would bypass `normalizeFontSize`/`normalizeLineHeight` document-wide, so losing the call — e.g. a future refactor restoring the bare `JSON.parse` — would be invisible to the suite.
searchedFor: read named-styles.test.ts additions in the diff

samples.summary: Slides store write paths other than `withTextElement` gained `bandBlockNumerics` with no test
samples.evidence: The new frontend slides tests cover `read()` for text/shape/table/notes and the write bridge for `withTextElement` only ('hands the editor bridge a banded body'). `withShapeText` (priorBlocks), `setNotes`/notes update and `withTableCellBody` also gained `bandBlockNumerics` calls; the pre-existing `describe('YorkieSlidesStore — withShapeText')` block (line 623) asserts nothing about banding. A dropped band on those write paths would carry a peer's poisoned value forward on the next edit and no test would notice.
searchedFor: read the added 'the text-body numeric band' describe block in the diff

samples.summary: The `if (!(fragHeight > 0)) fragHeight = remaining;` floor is declared unreachable and has no test
samples.evidence: pagination.ts documents the line as "unreachable today (verified by making it throw against the whole suite)", while `table-row-split.test.ts`'s new negative-budget case claims it discriminates "the `pageAvail > 0` condition and the `fragHeight > 0` floor below it". The two comments cannot both be right; either way no test exercises the floor branch, so it is untested defensive code.
searchedFor: read pagination.ts hunk and table-row-split.test.ts hunk in the diff

samples.summary: `normalizeColumnRatio` and `MAX_COLUMN_RATIO` are newly exported from both entries but never asserted directly
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts` imports neither; grepping `packages/docs/test` for `normalizeColumnRatio|MAX_COLUMN_RATIO` returns no matches. The upper clamp is only observed indirectly through the backend slides spec (`[1e9,-1] → [MAX_COLUMN_RATIO, 0]`), and `parseColumnWidthsAttr`'s tests exercise only the drop/zero branches (`'1e400,0.5'`, `'-1,2'`), never the clamp.
searchedFor: read numeric-attrs.test.ts import list in the diff

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The store wires three bands the frontend tests never exercise: normalizeTableSpan at yorkie-doc-store.ts:460-461 (treeNodeToCell colSpan/rowSpan), parseColumnWidthsAttr at :480 (treeNodeToBlock cols), sanitizeDocStyles at :711 (readDocStyles, reached via getDocument at :686). The new band describe block (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3388-3499, file ends 3501) covers only fontSize, image size, cell padding, rowHeights and listLevel. Every other colSpan/rowSpan occurrence in the file is an applyCellSpan write/read-back with in-band values (2719-2914) read from the writing store's own cache — the block's own comment at 3384-3386 states that path never runs the parse; cols appears only as a valid round-trip at 1246-1250; there is no named-style/stylesJson test at all. I searched wider for a counterexample: all 13 frontend files referencing YorkieDocStore (merge-repro, editor-undo-selection, editor-step-selection-font-size-undo, apply-imported-content, two-user-docs-yorkie helper) have no styles/colSpan/cols/Infinity assertions; the concurrent integration file exercises colSpan (756-804) and cols (855-920) only with valid values; repo-wide grep for the three band helpers finds no frontend test naming them; and packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts:18 imports treeNodeToBlock from the engine's crdt-tree, i.e. the other copy, not the frontend store. So a band dropped or wired to the wrong field in the copy serving the live editor (Infinity rowSpan into expandCellRangeForMerges) would ship undetected: a real, user-visible coverage gap over behavior this diff introduces.
